name: Soil Moisture Levels
description: Variations in soil moisture can significantly impact robot movement and stability, leading to slower travel times or erratic paths.

name: Weed Density
description: Dense weed growth can cause obstacles and require more precise navigation, increasing travel time.

name: Crop Density & Variety
description: The density and variety of crops within the field can influence the robot's path – some areas may require more turns or deviation than others.

name: Sun Angle & Light Intensity
description: Changes in sun angle and intensity affect the robot's visual perception and possibly its path choice, potentially impacting travel time.

name: Obstacle Presence (Wind, Animals, etc.)
description: Even subtle wind or animal movement can cause the robot to veer off course, affecting travel time.

name: Slope & Terrain Variation
description: Steeper slopes and uneven terrain require more precise control and can cause faster travel.

name: Rain/Snowfall Conditions
description: Reduced visibility and potential for slippery surfaces can affect sensor performance and route choices.

name: Lighting Conditions (Color & Intensity)
description: Changes in lighting can affect the robot's visual interpretation of the field, potentially altering the path.

name: Weather Patterns (Wind Gusts)
description: Strong wind gusts can alter the robot’s path unexpectedly, requiring adjustments.

name: Robot Calibration/Accuracy
description: Inaccurate sensor readings or mapping can lead to incorrect route choices and increased travel time.

name: Path Selection Bias
description: The controller might be systematically favoring one route (Path 1 or 2) even when the multimodal data suggests a different optimal path.

name: GPS Signal Strength & Interference
description: Weak GPS signals or interference can hinder accurate positioning and route tracking.

name: Robotic Speed & Gait
description: A variable speed or gait pattern could be contributing to the multimodal data.

name: Camera Shake
description: Camera movement can introduce noise to sensor data and alter the robot’s path.

name: Dynamic Field Conditions (Changes in slope/surface)
description: The field itself is not static; it’s changing, affecting the optimal route.
